clips.send: A parent sends it to whoever just finished a round of antibiotics - why the sugar cravings started right after, and the worry of what's really going on in their gut.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau connects a habit most people brush off - sugar cravings, bloating, gas - back to one root cause: Candida yeast overgrowth.

Antibiotics kill bacteria, which is the point when you're sick. But they don't just kill the bad bacteria - they wipe out good flora in the gut too. Candida, a yeast that's normally kept in check, moves in and overgrows, he says, and it feeds on sugar.

His view: if you crave bread, wine or dairy more than you used to, or deal with gas and bloating, it's worth asking whether gut yeast - not willpower - is driving it.

Have you taken antibiotics in the last year?
